claims: ... the second marginal rate fell from 16% to 15% on 1 July 2026 (also line 76: income between $18,201 and $45,000, line 52: 2% Medicare levy, line 68: 12% superannuation guarantee, line 64: 28 days)
whys: The figures look correct, but they are typed into the FAQ text instead of coming from constants, so they will not update when the payg-withholding constants change. Also, 'second marginal rate' counts the 0% band as the first rate. Readers may expect this to be called the first taxed rate.
constants: lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts (FY2026-27 rate note at line 24); super guarantee rate constant in lib/constants

claims: Every amount in the standard columns has the 2% Medicare levy built in, including the low-income shading that phases it in rather than applying it from the first dollar.
whys: The 'standard columns' include the no-tax-free-threshold column (Scale 1). The low-income Medicare levy phase-in is normally a feature of the threshold-claimed scale (Scale 2), so 'every amount ... including the low-income shading' may be too broad for Scale 1. Please check this against the SCALE_1_NO_TFT coefficients.
reviewerNotes: The writer's Medicare question about Scale 1 is unchanged text, so I left it as a fact question. Scale 1 (SCALE_1_NO_TFT) has its own middle bands, so a phase-in for no-threshold payees is plausible. The owner should confirm it against ATO Schedule 1 before narrowing the claim.

claims: Nothing is withheld until fortnightly earnings pass roughly {formatAUD(724)}
whys: $724 is typed into the source by hand. It is correct for 2026-27 (2 x 362) but does not change when the year toggle shows 2025-26, where the edge is 2 x 361 = $722.
$724 is typed into the source by hand and stays the same when the year toggle shows 2025-26. It should come from the SCALE_2 tax-free-threshold coefficient table in lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts.
constants: Derive it from SCALE_2_TFT[0].lessThan * 2 in lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts

claims: withholding falls by up to about {formatAUD(268 / 26)} per fortnight
whys: The $268 annual saving and the 2025-26 / 1 July 2026 / 1 July 2027 / 14% figures are typed into the prose instead of using PAYG_FINANCIAL_YEAR or PAYG constants. They will go stale at the next rollover.

claims: From 1 July 2027 the 15% rate falls to 14% and the Working Australians Tax Offset of $250 begins (also '14% is legislated for 1 July 2027' at line 389)
whys: These figures and the date are typed into template prose on 3 pages, not taken from code. The 2027-28 rate and the $250 offset amount should be checked once against the legislation and then read from one source, so the prose cannot drift from the calculator.
constants: TAX_BRACKETS_2027_28 / a WATO constant in lib/constants (australian-tax.ts)
reviewerNotes: I accept the writer's fact question. The text says the rate falls to 14% from 1 July 2027 and that the $250 Working Australians Tax Offset begins then. Both figures are typed into template prose on the three 2026-27 pages, not read from a constant. They need checking against the legislation and then reading from one source in lib/constants.

claims: Same result as the ATO look-up table: cents are ignored and the Schedule 1 formula is applied exactly.
whys: The widget renders on the monthly pages too. For monthly pay the ATO says to enter earnings including cents (with the 33-cent rule), as monthly-tax-table-faqs.ts line 40 and monthly-tax-table.tsx line 176 say. So 'cents are ignored' is wrong for the monthly cycle. The note text should depend on the frequency.

Confirmed against the code: lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts lines 297-307 keep cents for monthly pay (they add 1c when the amount ends in 33c before multiplying by 3 and dividing by 13). Only weekly and fortnightly use Math.floor(gross). So on the monthly pages the note contradicts both the code and monthly-tax-table-faqs.ts line 40.
constants: lookup-widget.tsx note text should branch on the frequency (weekly/fortnightly ignore cents, monthly keeps cents with the 33-cent rule), matching how calculatePAYGWithholding in lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts handles monthly
reviewerNotes: Confirmed the writer's fact question. In lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts lines 297-307, monthly keeps cents (it adds 1c when the amount ends in 33c, then multiplies by 3 and divides by 13). Only weekly and fortnightly ignore cents. So 'cents are ignored' is wrong on the three monthly pages. The fix needs a frequency-dependent note in code, which this pass cannot make.
